overview: The Federated States of Micronesia is a country of more than 600 islands in the western Pacific. Its capital is Palikir, on the island of Pohnpei. It is made up of four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae. Micronesia became independent in 1986 and has a close association with the United States.

geography.text: The islands range from high volcanic islands such as Pohnpei and Kosrae, which are mountainous and covered in rainforest, to low coral atolls. Pohnpei is one of the wettest places on Earth. Off its coast lies Nan Madol, an ancient city of stone built on small artificial islands, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and very rainy; Pohnpei is one of the wettest places on Earth.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Coral reefs and the Pohnpei lorikeet.

history.text: The islands were settled by Micronesian voyagers, and from about the 1100s the stone city of Nan Madol was built off Pohnpei. The islands were later ruled by Spain, Germany and Japan, and after the Second World War by the United States as a UN trust territory. Micronesia became independent in 1986, in free association with the US.

events.title: US trust territory

government.text: The Federated States of Micronesia is a federation of four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae. Its Congress elects the President from among its members. It has a Compact of Free Association with the United States, which provides defence and funding.

economy.text: US aid, fishing licences and government jobs make up much of the economy. Most people live from farming and fishing.

culture.text: Each of the four states has its own language and customs. Yap is famous for its giant stone money discs, some taller than a person, which are still used in traditional exchanges. Nan Madol, a ruined city of stone islets off Pohnpei, is a UNESCO site.

items.title: Nan Madol
items.text: Stone buildings on nearly 100 artificial islets.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Sakau, a kava drink, is shared in ceremonies on Pohnpei.

sport.text: Basketball, volleyball and athletics are popular. The Micronesian Games bring together athletes from across the region every four years.

didYouKnow: Yap's giant stone coins, some taller than a person, are still used in traditional exchanges.
Nan Madol is sometimes called the 'Venice of the Pacific'.
